title: Comparing Magnitudes & Fractional Reductions: kétszer akkora, felére esik

sections.title: Comparative Magnitude Multipliers: kétszer akkora / háromszor annyi
sections.content: Hungarian combines numerical multipliers with demonstrative pro-adjectives and pro-adverbs to express comparative magnitude: 'kétszer akkora, mint...' ('twice as large as...'), 'háromszor annyi, mint...' ('three times as much/many as...'). Notice that 'akkora' corresponds to physical size, spatial volume, or conceptual magnitude, while 'annyi' corresponds strictly to countable or quantifiable amounts.

sections.title: Fractional Contraction in Sublative: a felére / harmadára csökken
sections.content: When values contract or shrink, Hungarian uses the sublative of the fraction noun: 'a felére csökken' ('falls to half / is halved'), 'a harmadára esik vissza' ('drops to a third'), 'a töredékére zsugorodik' ('shrinks to a fraction of its former size'). In financial reporting, this construction pairs with verbs of shrinkage: 'apad', 'zsugorodik', 'zuhan', 'esik'.

items.spanish: Az idei költségvetési hiány kétszer akkora, mint a tavalyi év azonos időszakában volt.
items.english: This year's budget deficit is twice as large as it was in the same period of last year.

items.spanish: A drasztikus takarékossági intézkedések nyomán a működési kiadások a felükre csökkentek.
items.english: Following drastic austerity measures, operating expenses were reduced to half.

items.spanish: A bank háromszor annyi hitelkérelmet utasított el a szigorúbb fedezeti követelmények miatt.
items.english: The bank rejected three times as many loan applications due to stricter collateral requirements.

items.spanish: A részvények értéke a pénzügyi botrány kirobbanása után a harmadára zuhant a tőzsdén.
items.english: The value of the shares plunged to a third on the stock exchange after the outbreak of the financial scandal.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: Pay close attention: 'kétszer akkora' means 200% the size, while 'a felére csökkent' means it contracted down to 50%. Always put the fraction in the sublative (-ra/-re).
